utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were no buses parked in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever see any traffic of buses or trucks carrying passengers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But that was on the 12th. I did see a couple of buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who was in the buses.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were people on those buses. I was standing outside the health centre, and that's where I saw them pass by. But the distance between the health centre and the road they took must be at least about 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone inform you as to who was in those buses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn who was in those buses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later. When the whole thing happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many buses exactly you would have seen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time of day that would have been? These are all questions that the Prosecution I'm sure is keen to ask, which is why I'm asking them.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It was throughout the day. But it could have been at about 12.00 or 1.00 p.m., or thereabouts. It's been a long time, after all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 13th, I failed to ask you whether you had ventured into Potocari.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So not on the 12th and not on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us whether you had heard about an incident that occurred at the Kravica agricultural warehouse? Would you have heard about it? And we're going to go step by step. Have you ever --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I heard nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So do you know -- as you sit here today, do you know whether something happened at that Kravica warehouse? I'm not saying whether you saw it, or that you were there when it was occurring, but whether you have learned of an incident?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Later, four or five days later after that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you learn who was involved in that incident?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about visiting the Muslim men that were at the school, the Vuk Karadzic school, on the 13th, when you had been ordered by your commander to see if anyone needed some medical treatment that you were able to dispense. Could you please tell us, if you know, what happened to those people.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that they were driven towards Kladanj, Zvornik, and so on. That's what I heard, that most of them were to be exchanged. I don't know their final destination. I did hear about it later on, but that was sometime after. I did hear what had had happened to those people, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear had happened to those people?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that most of them had been killed, that they had ended up in Zvornik, those villages over there. That sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the 14th of July, do you recall what you did for the rest of the week, the 15th, the 16th, the 17th? Do you recall if there was anything unusual that sticks out in your mind as you've told us about the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not much. Those were very ordinary days. After all of that, I was expecting every day to be called up to return to work where I used to work, the company. That sort of thing. There was no combat activity, no tension, no fear any more. Everything was sort of back to normal in the town itself there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was it back to normal?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in some way people were no longer -- well, there you have it. They were no longer afraid. They were no longer afraid of shooting. They believed that the whole thing was finally over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we know, and it has been established, that at some point, the 17th of July, in fact, a portion of -- the majority of the Bratunac Brigade went off to Zepa. Did you by any chance go off there to that location?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually return back to work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I went back to work. I was in Bratunac, spent some time at the command, some time at the health centre. And that's how time went by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much longer were you in the Bratunac Brigade before you went back to work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly the date when I left, but I had a little problem because there was no one to hand the storage room over to, or the remainder of the medicines that were being kept there. I did go back to work, however, but I still kept the key with me. I believe it was a month and a half or two months later that I handed the key over and returned my equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to show you a document that has previously been admitted as D165. If you could help us out here, if you could please just look at this document first, just look at it. And I will walk you through step by step with some questions. No drama. Do you see this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document, and I'm referring, again, for the record, to D165, purports to be notes from a working meeting of commanders with command staff and battalion commanders. Do you see that at the top?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, we have a date, and the date is 16 October 1995.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you see your name in this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's where it says that -- talks about those who attended. We see Nikolic, that would have been Momir, Micic, Trisic, Cvjetinovic, Jovanovic, Beatovic, Petrovic, and Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, you were within the post or the unit of the rear services. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we've already established that Mr. Trisic was your commanding officer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the commanding officer is there, why would you also be at this particular meeting, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: The reason for my attendance, for me being there with my superior commander Trisic was that I would usually report on the problems in terms of our medical work, the shortage of medicines and the rest. I would report in detail. I would go there to attend for Mr. Blagojevic, to hear it personally. That was the purpose of my being there. May I continue now? May I continue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead, since you're on a roll.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because very often, at such meetings, I would be criticised by battalion commanders because the soldiers often took ill. There were too few soldiers along the front lines, and they would criticise me as though it was something that I tolerated or if I allowed the soldiers to do so. Therefore, I needed to be personally present there in order to deny false accusations. I wouldn't say for too long at those meetings, and I believe that that was not my place to be after all. It was only in exceptional cases that I came. After all, my superior commander was there at those meetings, and I believed there was no need for me to be there, too. So much for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that full explanation. Now, I just want to draw your attention to one matter in this document, and then I believe we're pretty much through. If we look at the bottom of the page, the last item where we have Nikolic, I believe these are Mr. Nikolic's notes, it says here: "We are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska General Staff" and in parenthesis, it says "sanitation," or the way he has put it is: "Asanacija." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Asanacija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall this being mentioned at that meeting, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot help us out here as to what, if anything, Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, okay. Well, I needed to get that out of the way. As I said. No drama. I want to thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions. I believe there may be some questions, though I doubt it, from Mr. Jokic's attorney. The Prosecution perhaps, and maybe even from the Judges. I want to thank you for being frank and honest with me, and I would hope that you could be as frank and honest with them as you have been with me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Beatovic. Your Honours, we have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. I do have a few questions. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Sir, I believe in your examination-in-chief, you said that before the 6th of July, you were not aware of the pending attack on Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is you had no idea that Srebrenica was going to be attacked until it actually fell before the fall of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when precisely did you know, just to clarify, that Srebrenica was, in fact, attacked?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 11th.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to that, you hadn't heard anything?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to take you, sir, to your transcript. I'll give you a copy in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the B/C/S version, sir, I'd like you to turn to page 5 starting at line 17. Then we're going to go through to page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In English, Your Honour, we're at page 5, starting at about line 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll just read it slowly. Line 18, sir, you say in response to a question whether it was the 12th or the 14th, where would you have been at that period, where were you on those two days? You say: "I heard maybe a few days before. I heard that there will be an attack on Srebrenica, that they were supposed to do that, an attack on Srebrenica. However, that day, I was at the health centre. One of the nurses asked me, so what's going on? Has Srebrenica fallen already? And I told her I have no idea." And then the question goes on. And it says: "Okay. And who told you or how did you find out a few days before Srebrenica there would be an attack?" And your answer is: "It was a rumour. Everybody was talking about it. People were talking about it. It was city stories."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know whether I'm reading from the same text. But on line 21, it says "I told her I have no idea. And around 12.00, I heard that they entered Srebrenica." And this could give the impression, at least, that this conversation is taking place on the 11th, at least -- and that portion wasn't read by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was building up to the second part of the next question, and I think I was trying to put it into context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, what's your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My objection is if she is going to read his answer, not to skip over the vital aspect of the answer that is critical to what he's saying. She skipped the portion that said "I have no idea," and then he goes on, "and around 12.00 I heard that they entered Srebrenica." That's the portion that somehow, coincidentally, rather intentionally, was omitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, really, that is just -- that's an outrageous allegation. We all have the text in front of us. It's clear from the text that, you know, he was talking about the 11th when he said: "However that day I was at the health centre and continued on." The investigator continued with the next question to clarify it and asked him about the few days before that, and that's what I was getting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think you're too soon to make your objection. I believe Ms. Issa would like to walk this witness through the whole page. Eventually she will come to that vital aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hopefully, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's what you told the investigators at that time, sir. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. I'm not sure what the question is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was what you told the investigators, what I just read out. Those were your answers. You were asked those questions and you gave those answers. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: What I said is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying now that you had heard about the attack on Srebrenica a few days before the attack actually took place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. No, not a few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But isn't that what you were asked by the investigator in Banja Luka on December -- in December 2001?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, you answered that it was a rumour. Everybody was talking about it and people were talking about it. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, people were talking about it in town. But that was all unofficial. It was almost as if the birds were singing that tune, but that was nothing official.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say it was almost as though the birds were singing that tune, what you're really telling us, sir, is that everybody knew about it. It was such common knowledge that even the birds knew. Right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't quite like that. But... I'm not sure what to say now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm simply repeating your answer when you just told us a moment ago, when you said it was like the birds singing the tune. And I understood that to mean that it was pretty common knowledge, wasn't it? Yeah?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, people know everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to something else. Now, when you were interviewed by the investigators in December of 2001, you never told them, you never mentioned that on 13 July, Colonel Blagojevic told you to check on the prisoners, did you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No. Because in some way, that question was not asked. What happened in Banja Luka, this is -- well, how should I know? There were no questions about anything really serious. I think what was mentioned is that I had given a statement and that I had gone there, but I did not mention General Blagojevic. Had there been no order for me to go, I could not have gone there in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the transcript. If we can turn to page 14 in the English version, at about line 7; page 16 for you, sir, line 27 until the end, and then up to page 17. And you were asked the following questions: Question: "Were you aware that many hundreds of Muslim men were held prisoners in Bratunac in the school, in the halls and hangars and buildings?" Your answer was: "No." Question: "Are you sure?" Answer: "Yes, I'm sure." Do you remember telling the investigator, sir, that you had no idea that there were Muslim prisoners in the schools?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where it says that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to page 16 --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: What page is that? 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Line 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would ask that he be given an opportunity to read the previous portion, and the previous portion be read by the Prosecutor for context purposes. Because it's being taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't see how this has been taken out of context, Your Honour. It's pretty clear. But in any event, we can give the gentleman the opportunity to read that to himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which item?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 16, sir, line 27 and following.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I knew about the school, the Vuk Karadzic school. About the other one, I didn't know about that one. What I thought was that there was a minor group of people, something like that. As for the hangars and all of that, I really didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you were specifically asked about a school, halls, hangars, and buildings. That's a pretty general question. And you said you were sure you had no idea. Now, it goes on, and the question after that says: "Many people in Bratunac knew this. Thousands of men held prisoners."

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you asked: "Where could they put them if there were thousands?" And the answer that the investigator gave you: "Buses and trucks in the street. See the photo I showed you. Vuk Karadzic school. The hangar of Vuk Karadzic school. Did you know about it?" And you say: "No, I saw them here passing by. This is what I refer when they" - then it's unintelligible - "this is what I've seen, going towards Vlasenica and Kladanj." Nowhere there, sir, do you say that your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, told you to check on the prisoners at the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Where is it, and I would like the Prosecutor to show us, where is it that he is specifically asked about going there? The question wasn't posed, and the gentleman said, since it wasn't posed, he didn't give any answer. Now she's trying to twist and turn. If she can show me where the question was posed and where the gentleman declined to give a truthful answer, I would like that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, that I believe the Prosecutor recited whatever in that previous statement. And the question asked by the investigator at that time was a very general question. If this gentleman had said that he knew nothing about the prisoners in those schools, hangars, you know, in the Bratunac town, so there's no need to ask the follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll walk the gentleman through his statement in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I believe that Ms. Issa will leave some contents for your redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think it's more than that, Your Honour. I think I need to be fair with the gentleman. That's what I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you went inside the school on the 13th of July, did you see bodies there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I saw people. They were still alive. I didn't see bodies. No one had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone seriously or almost mortally wounded there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the 50 bodies that were found inside the classrooms in the school, in and around the Vuk Karadzic school on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. They weren't found on the 13th of July, and I would like to know from what part of the record the Prosecution is reading from. Where has it been established that on the 13th of July that they were found there? Again, it would seem to be making up facts, Your Honour. I think we need to be fair with these witnesses. After the prisoners left, we heard testimony, that's when bodies were found, and that's when there was asanacija. I think it's mischaracterising the evidence, and we're trying to turn this witness into a liar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the witness has already answered the question. So it's over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you. But I would like, at least when this particular Prosecutor conducts her examination, not just to state facts off the top of her head, but rather to pinpoint, because there seems to be a tendency, inadvertently or advertently, to try to mischaracterise the evidence. And I find it difficult to just sit here like a potted plant and not react.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe Ms. Issa will put the evidence as precise as possible to this witness in the future. But Witness, would you please repeat your answer. I don't think the transcript reflected it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see any bodies there at the time, when I entered the school because there had been no killings of any sort at that time. If you refer to bodies that were found around the school, that was perhaps after my departure. But there was no shooting. I would have heard something like that. There was nothing. I don't know what bodies you are talking about. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me clarify it, sir, then. The question was were you aware that there were bodies that were found at that school in the classrooms, around the school?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you never heard about that after the fact?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware whether Muslims in the school were being beaten and abused?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't the Muslims, when you got there, ask you for food or water?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there were buses parked all over Bratunac on the 12th and 13th of July, including near the Vuk Karadzic school. Did you not see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing which I saw is that the -- when the buses were leaving Srebrenica, they were making a turn in the centre of Vlasenica -- in the centre of Bratunac towards Vlasenica and Kladanj. But where they were parked, I don't know. Probably they were also parked by the school saying that there were Muslims prisoners in the school. They didn't park any buses in the centre of the city; perhaps in the periphery or in some other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you never saw them parked there with the Muslim men inside the buses around Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Not in the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Getting back to the earlier point of going to the school, you were asked on page 13, line 8, a question, I think for you it would be around page 7: "So in the ten days" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, let the witness please find the location. Let's be fair to the witness. Let's be fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is totally unnecessary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, for the convenience of the witness. Witness, did you find the right page and right line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 13, did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Number 6. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Prosecutor indicated that she, I think for you, it would be around page 7, which is why I reacted, because the pages are not that far off.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I should have said line 7, Your Honour. And I misspoke. But I think before I was able to correct myself, Mr. Karnavas jumped up. In the English translation, it's on page 13 at line 8. And unfortunately, I don't happen to have the precise line in the B/C/S version. But I believe it's on page 12 in the B/C/S version. Perhaps what might speed up the process, Your Honour, and this is what I was going to suggest also, perhaps if I can simply read it in the English version into the record, and then we can give the gentleman an opportunity to look for it if he wishes to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question: "So in the ten days from the fall of Srebrenica, did you go anywhere except the health centre and the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?" And you said: "No. There was no need for that. After all of that, when they started removing people, there were buses and trucks, people passing by. I saw the buses full. The trucks, people on trucks, I really removed, walked away. I was afraid because a lot of Muslims knew me, and I didn't want them to say the next day, 'Oh, I saw Ljubo there as well,' so I didn't." Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were asked specifically by the investigator whether after the fall of Srebrenica you went anywhere, aside from the health centre in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not "and the Bratunac," but "in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I did say the word "in," Your Honour. Perhaps Mr. Karnavas can listen more carefully. And it's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I see the transcript, and I'm listening very carefully, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you see there, sir, you were asked a specific question. And when you were asked whether you went anywhere aside from that location, you never told the investigator that you went to the Vuk Karadzic school pursuant to orders by Colonel Blagojevic, did you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go to the last area, Your Honour. I don't know when you wish to take the break. I only have a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We may proceed until we finish this witness, if we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I did not, you know, prejudge in the time the redirect will use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we do leave this area, you also told investigators, sir, that in fact you hadn't had much contact with Blagojevic during those days.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, getting back to the meeting, of October 16, and drawing your attention again to the very last line of that meeting, D165/1 for the record, do you have that document in front of you, sir? I wonder if perhaps the witness can be provided -- thank you very much, Madam Usher. Now, you see that last line there, sir, that was read out to you in the examination-in-chief? Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that specifically states that "we are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska General Staff, asanacija." That states that they were at the time referring to the word "currently" engaged in tasks of asanacija. You don't recall that happening at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No. I attended this meeting, but it is also quite possible that I left early. And I do not remember this particular note, this particular record that that was mentioned at the time, this reference which you made. Perhaps I had left the meeting early. From this particular record, I only remember that it referred to soldiers, the supply of wood and uniforms and things of that kind, because I insisted for the families of the soldiers to be supplied with fuel and wood. As regards this thing discussed under item 3, I have no recollection whatsoever of it. That was a long time ago. And frankly speaking, I cannot give you any comment on it because I do not remember anything in regard of that particular case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware of the decomposing bodies that were driven through Bratunac at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't smell anything in the town during those days?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard about it at that time from another source aside from the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the Muslim prisoners at the health centre, brought to the health centre, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. In fact, I arrived there, and I believe that is also mentioned in the statement. I came this one day. I don't remember the date. I came to the health centre and entered the storage room where I kept my medicines and had this tiny office. In the hall, there were about four or five of them. And among them was an acquaintance of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What day was this? What day was this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Before. I think it was before the fall, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm asking you, sir, whether or not you were aware of Muslim prisoners brought to the health centre.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually telling you about these five men that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about after the fall of Srebrenica, just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't believe I have anything further, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, and I think we can keep it rather short. Just try to put matters into context for fairness. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could direct the gentleman to his statement, this would be page 5 at around line 11. And for us in English, it would be page 5, line 9. Do we have an extra one for the ELMO? I want to apologise to the translation booth for not having one for the ELMO. I'll go slow. Maybe we can put the B/C/S on the ELMO, and then the gentleman can read from the screen. I just want to make it convenient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could -- I'm going to go down, and I'm going to read a portion of it. Now, it states here, you were asked some questions as to -- about knowing about the events of Srebrenica, when they commenced and when Srebrenica fell. Now, please correct me if I'm wrong. Do you recall being asked: "So I'm specifically interested in the period just before Srebrenica fell and afterwards. Do you recall when Srebrenica fell?" Your answer was: "I don't know if it was 12 or 14." Question: "Of?" "I think July." "What year?" It says: "1995." "Whether it was the 12th or the 14th, where would you have been at that period? Where were you on those two days?" And you state: "I heard maybe a few days before, I heard that there would be an attack on Srebrenica, that they were supposed to do that, an attack on Srebrenica. However, that day I was at the health centre. One of the nurses asked me, 'So, what's going on? Has Srebrenica fallen already?' And I told her, 'I have no idea.' At around 12.00, I heard that they entered Srebrenica." Next question: "Okay. And who told you or how did you find out a few days before Srebrenica there would be an attack?" And you state: "It was a rumour. Everybody was talking about it. People were talking about it. It was city stories." In your statement here, sir, it would appear, would it not, that you had heard rumours and had not heard it from anyone at the command post. Would that be a fair assessment of what you said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is totally leading. Mr. Karnavas knows that that would be an improper form of the question in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think it's totally proper, Your Honour. I'm trying to put it into context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we have heard this evidence in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll go on to the next one, Your Honour. I'll take it sequentially, in the manner in which these questions were posed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were read a portion of your statement on page 14. I want to direct your attention, this would be page 16, and I'm going to be looking at lines 23 to 25. That's in the Srpski version, or B/C/S as we say here. And for us, it would be 14. I'm going to start actually on line 1, just so we have context. Dean Manning: "Do you recall the period when buses and trucks full of men were parked in Bratunac, full of prisoners in Bratunac?" And your answer is: "They went one after another, and they were making turns and going towards Vlasenica." Question: "And how long did this continue for? Hours or days?" Your answer is, in English is: "I don't know what to tell you. But it seems to me it was done just one day." Now, in your version, could you please read out slowly what you told Dean Manning when Dean Manning asked you: "How long did this continue for, hours or days?" What was your response? That would be line 23 to 25, could you please read out those lines on page 16.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: What I told him, and I was slightly vulgar, in fact --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just read out what you said.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: "Well, I don't know." And then I used this vulgar phrase and said: "What shall I tell you? I believe this was only that one day. And I believe that it was just that day. And that's how it was. So it wasn't a number of days, no. This was just that one day." Then he asked me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to go to the next question. I just wanted to make sure that we had a full record because it's not reflected in the translation that we were provided, at least the draft transcript. I don't know if it was corrected in the other one. But it would give us at least your full answer. Now, you were then asked: "Were you aware that many hundreds of Muslim were held prisoner in Bratunac in the schools and in the halls and hangars and buildings?" Sir, when you were asked that question, do you know whether the gentleman was referring as to whether you were aware at that time or whether you were aware at the time when the Prosecution got around to come to questioning you, which would have been 2 December 2001, close to two years after they had indicted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all it's totally leading and it doesn't really arise out of the cross-examination. I mean, I don't think that was the point. But it's completely leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this paragraph was read out by you to this witness. And Mr. Karnavas raises a very interesting question. We would like to hear how the witness is going to answer it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the question was posed to you, how did you understand that question to be? Was it that you were aware at the time, that is, back in July 1995, or whether you were aware at the time you were being questioned on 2001? How did you understand his question?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that in July 1995. But I didn't know that the prisoners were on a number of sites such as the hangars, the buildings, et cetera. I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you become aware? Was it when they were actually physically in those places or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: I became aware when I went there to see those people, but before that I didn't know that they were there. That was in 1995, after they had been brought there from Srebrenica. And I just went to the school to see these people. And as for these other people indicated here as being in various different places, in these hangars, I didn't know about those. I only went to the school. I didn't know that there were any other people or that there were more people in these other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One last area: I want to go to page 13. This would be page 15 in your case. And I'm going to be reading from page 13, line 1. And for you, it would be page 15, it will be somewhere around line 10. Perhaps a little earlier. You're posed a question. This is line 3 actually. "When Srebrenica fell, did you go to Potocari?"

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm reading from the transcript. We heard you, and now you told them that at the same time. But let me continue. I just want to make sure we get it into context. So your answer was no. Then you were asked: "Not at all during that, say, ten-day period after Srebrenica fell?" Answer: "No. No one asked me to because battalions, every battalion had their own medics, so if someone went there, they went." Then the next question is: "So, in the ten days from the fall of Srebrenica, did you go anywhere except in the health centre in or and the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?" Then you give the answer: "No, there was no need for that. After all..." And then so on. When you were asked that question, when you were asked that question, so in the ten days from the fall of Srebrenica, did you go anywhere, in light of the previous questions, how did you understand that question? Was it whether you had --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is outrageous. He's just -- it's totally leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't finished the question. It's outrageous that I'm being interrupted by the Prosecutor. She posed this question. She wants to take it out of context. The gentleman is entitled to give an explanation how he understood the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let the witness answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the question was being posed in light of the previous questions as to whether you had gone to Potocari, did you understand his question to be whether you had gone anywhere in Bratunac, or whether you had gone to Potocari or elsewhere outside of Bratunac? How did you understand his question? In reading the sequencing in the manner in which Dean Manning was posing them?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karnavas is essentially testifying now. He's pointing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand. It's all in the transcript. Do you see that? I want to hear how the witness will answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I did not go to Potocari. I was, as written here, in Bratunac in the command, in the health centre. That was the area within which I moved. I didn't go outside Bratunac or anywhere else, and I felt there was no need for me to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you point anywhere in your transcript where Dean Manning asked you concretely whether you went anywhere inside Bratunac other than the health centre and the brigade command? Concretely, which as I understand is the way people speak in that country.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes I would spend more time at home. And there you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, had Mr. Manning, when questioning you, asked you whether you had gone anywhere within Bratunac, would you have informed him about --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question. If -- assuming he wanted to ask you as to whether you had been anywhere inside Bratunac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is assuming. This is out of the scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. It's very clear from the question, though, that it was never asked concretely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one last question: Have you any reasons to lie for Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR BEATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This question is also out of the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I believe, Your Honour, it's slightly in the scope in light of what was being insinuated, that he fabricated this whole notion about being told to go to the health centre. So I think it's tangentially --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your next question, if you have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have none, Your Honour, that was my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. When the Court is adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. The hearing is adjourned until next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
